summary.intent: Run the GSD manager to discuss, plan, and begin executing all 5 hardening phases (51-55) of the CipherBox v1.1 milestone in parallel, then fully ship Phase 51 through the complete verify → secure → validate → simplify → CodeRabbit → ship → resolve-reviews loop.
summary.outcome: All 5 phases discussed and planned in parallel using isolated git worktrees; Phase 51 executed, shipped as PR #529 (merged to main with 3 fix commits after finding a real regression and addressing CodeRabbit findings); a reusable `/ship-phase` command created to automate future post-execution steps.

repo: GSD executor's `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` gate never compiles crates/sdk or apps/desktop — cross-crate consumers of crypto type changes silently break

GSD commit style 'feat NN: message' is non-conventional; repo's Release Preview CI enforcement rejects space+digit before the colon — bulk-reword required via `git filter-branch --msg-filter 'sed -E "1 s/^([a-z]+) [0-9][0-9A-Za-z.-]*: /\1: /"'`
git push requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` — the Claude Code sandbox blocks git egress to github.com even though curl works fine
GSD commit helper reports `commit_failed` as a false negative — always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never retry based on helper output
#683 auto-degrade fires when worktree HEAD diverges from origin/HEAD, forcing sequential execute-phase in-tree — sidesteps per-plan sub-worktree node_modules problems entirely
Background agents on this harness (general-purpose/claude) have `Tools: *` including the Agent tool — nesting subagents in background works, contradicting the manager.md guardrail
`winfsp` cannot compile on macOS (winfsp-sys build script + windows_core) — Windows-gated Rust changes must rely on CI for gate correctness
CodeRabbit PR nitpicks are bundled in the review body, not inline threads — `gh api pulls/N/comments` returns 0; must fetch review body via `/reviews` endpoint
Phase 55 (lib.rs decomposition) must execute AFTER phases 51+52 land on main — all three touch crates/fuse/src/lib.rs and a pre-merge refactor would make the eventual merge brutal
SDK E2E suite is the only cross-package gate that catches boundary changes between packages — unit suites mock the boundary and miss cascading type changes

code.finding: S3 zeroization added `params.ipnsPrivateKey.fill(0)` in finally — but cas.ts passes a reused, caller-owned buffer across retries and mutations; second publish derived pubkey from zeros → 400 'publicKey does not correspond to the given ipnsName', causing 48/89 SDK E2E failures. Rule: callees must never zero caller-owned buffers.

S3's `unwrap_key` return-type change to `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` cascaded to this desktop consumer; the executor's `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` gate never compiled the desktop crate, so it shipped as a build break. Fixed first with `.to_vec()`, then properly by making the SDK-state field `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`.
Field `root_folder_key` changed from `RwLock<Option<Vec<u8>>>` to `RwLock<Option<zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>>` to address CodeRabbit finding #3 — long-lived session key was stored unzeroized.

S2 fail-closed check `if (signatureV2 || data || pubKey)` treated empty-string fields as absent — all-empty record would downgrade to legacy allow path. Must use nullish checks instead of truthiness for security gates on string fields.
Production 404 catch only checked `error.status`; real axios 404s arrive as `error.response?.status` — live 404s would throw instead of returning null. sdk-core already handled both shapes correctly.

Folder-key cache `HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>` stored unzeroized keys with a misleading 'cleared when dropped' comment; changed to `HashMap<String, Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>` (CodeRabbit #6). The cache correctly returns `Vec<u8>` to callers to preserve the existing call contract.
Three identical base64 decode-and-map-err blocks consolidated into a local closure via the simplify pass — only non-trivial cleanup found in the branch diff.
Documents the key-ownership contract explicitly: 'publishWithCas NEVER zeroes... callers are responsible' — confirms the S3 zeroization placement was architecturally wrong.

workflow: Worktree isolation pattern for parallel GSD agents: `git worktree add <path> <branch>` + `pnpm i` in each worktree + no node_modules symlinks — clean isolation, hooks still run via absolute core.hooksPath
Discuss next phase inline while previous phases plan in background agents — maximizes throughput; the single constraint is avoiding concurrent git commits to the same files
Run CodeRabbit CLI review BEFORE ship (not after) so the PR opens already-clean — saves a fix-push cycle on obvious findings
After force-push, fetch/rebase before any further push — release-please bot may have pushed a chore(release) commit during CI

When a session-limit interruption cuts off a background agent mid-work, check `git log` on the worktree and the task output file before relaunching — the agent may have committed successfully before being cut off
`cargo fmt` can reformat entire pre-existing files when applied to a single changed function — apply changes manually without `cargo fmt` on whole files to avoid unrelated churn in the PR diff

Adversarial workflow verification pattern (3 independent agents each trying to refute a fix) catches subtle leaks that a single verifier misses, especially for security changes with multiple interaction surfaces

friction: Two session-limit interruptions required manual detection of agent state (git log check) and re-launch with reconstructed context
git push was blocked by the Claude Code sandbox — required `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on every push in the session
GSD executor commit style breaks repo's conventional commit enforcement — required bulk reword of 13 commits via git filter-branch before CI could pass
SDK E2E regression (48/89 failures) was only discovered after PR opened — the unit suites all passed because they mocked the cross-package boundary that the real failure occurred at
CodeRabbit re-reviewed my own fix commits and found new gaps in them, requiring a third fix commit — total of 3 fix commits before PR was mergeable
GitHub API timeouts during thread-resolve loop required idempotent retry logic to avoid duplicate replies
`cargo fmt` reflowed entire `crates/fuse/mod.rs` (283-line diff) when applying a 2-line change — had to revert and re-apply manually to avoid churn
Phase 51 planner was initially launched without worktree isolation, sharing the main working tree — caught mid-flight and required stopping, re-isolating, and restarting
The PR title format `Phase 51: <slug>` would fail `lint-pr-title` CI — required a custom conventional-commits title
winfsp Rust code cannot be compiled or tested on macOS, requiring trust in CI for correctness of Windows-gated changes
